subject: general
question: What is the primary purpose of shielding in electrical cables?

options.text: To increase the current-carrying capacity of the cable
To protect the cable from external electromagnetic interference
To increase the voltage capacity of the cable
To prevent heat loss from the cable

solution:
The correct answer is __To protect the cable from external electromagnetic interference**(Option 2)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Shielding__ in electrical cables is used to minimize electromagnetic interference (EMI).
 
• It protects the signal integrity by reducing external interference.
 
• Shielding also prevents the cable from emitting electromagnetic signals that may interfere with other devices.
 
• Typical materials used for shielding include metal foil or braided wire.
 
• It is particularly important in environments with high electromagnetic activity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Electromagnetic Interference (EMI):**
 
 
• EMI is a disturbance generated by external electromagnetic sources that affect electrical circuits.
 
• Proper shielding in cables helps mitigate these disturbances.
 
 
 
• **Types of Shielding:**
 
 
• Foil shielding: Thin layers of aluminum to block EMI.
 
• Braid shielding: Woven copper strands providing mechanical strength and EMI protection.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Used in communication cables, audio cables, and power cables in sensitive environments.
 
• Ensures reliable signal transmission and device functionality.
